payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-08-28
payload.summary:
**Voice agents are getting very real**; **ChatGPT is pushing deeper into real-world tasks** while Google pitches Gemini as the year of voice; Anthropic swings from safety theory to product surface with containment architecture and live artifacts.

**The mood split is sharp**; Sam Altman sounds a cyber-defense alarm, Aaron Levie argues software and agents rise together, and Ryan Greenblatt’s 2029 takeover timeline drags the alignment fight back into the center.

**语音代理开始落地了**；**ChatGPT** 往买菜、打车、预约这些真任务里钻，**Google** 也把 **Gemini** 往“开口就干活”的路上猛推；**Anthropic** 一边摊开讲怎么关住 **Claude**，一边把可分享的 artifacts 端上桌。

**今天的气氛很分裂**；**Sam Altman** 直接敲响 AI 网络防御警报，**Aaron Levie** 继续押注软件系统和 agents 绑在一起长，另一头 **Ryan Greenblatt** 把“2029 接管风险”又硬生生拽回台前。

items.person_name: The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck

sections.headline: **Ryan Greenblatt** warns the superintelligence race could break bad by 2029; **Ryan Greenblatt** 警告超级智能竞赛最早可能在 2029 年失控
sections.body:
Matt Turck’s latest **MAD Podcast** episode is a dark, direct conversation with **Redwood Research** chief scientist **Ryan Greenblatt** about AI takeover risk, the **AI 2040 Plan A**, and why he thinks major lab CEOs understand the danger but are still pushing ahead. Greenblatt frames superintelligence not as inherently bad but as dangerous, especially if misaligned systems automate R&D, concentrate power, or outrun society’s ability to govern the resulting capabilities.

这期 **MAD Podcast** 找来 **Redwood Research** 首席科学家 **Ryan Greenblatt**，把话题直接拉到 AI 接管风险、**AI 2040 Plan A**，以及为什么他判断大模型公司 CEO 明知危险还在继续往前冲。Greenblatt 的核心说法不是“超级智能天然有害”，而是它很危险，尤其当错位系统开始自动化研发、把权力越收越紧，或者技术推进速度快到治理根本跟不上。

sections.headline: **Anthropic** lays out how it tries to keep **Claude** useful without blowing up the blast radius; **Anthropic** 摊开讲怎么让 **Claude** 能干活又别把风险放大
sections.body:
In a detailed engineering post, **Anthropic** argues that the real deployment problem is no longer whether models can do meaningful work, but how to contain the damage if they fail. The piece breaks agent risk into user misuse, model misbehavior, and external attack, then focuses on the environmental controls that matter most in practice: sandboxes, VMs, filesystem boundaries, egress controls, and tightly scoped tool access.

这篇工程长文的重点很明确：现在卡人的不只是模型能不能干活，而是出事时能把伤害圈多小。**Anthropic** 把 agent 风险拆成三类，分别是用户乱来、模型自己跑偏、外部攻击；真正下重手的防线则是运行环境本身，比如 sandbox、虚拟机、文件系统边界、出网限制，还有尽量抠细的工具权限。

sections.headline: **Claude Code** turns sessions into live artifacts you can share and keep updating; **Claude Code** 把会话直接变成可分享、可持续更新的 artifacts
sections.body:
**Claude Code** now supports artifacts: live visual pages generated from a working session that can become PR walkthroughs, incident timelines, dashboards, architecture explainers, or release checklists. The pitch is straightforward: instead of translating an agent session into status updates by hand, teams can publish a living page built from repo context, connectors, and the conversation itself, with version history and org-scoped access.

**Claude Code** 现在能把会话产出直接做成 artifacts，也就是会自己更新的可视化页面，适合拿来做 PR walkthrough、事故时间线、dashboard、架构说明或者发布清单。思路不绕：别再靠人手把 agent 的过程翻译成进度汇报，直接把代码库上下文、连接器数据和会话推理揉成一个活页面，带版本历史，权限也收在组织范围内。

sections.headline: New AI products may need to live inside top harnesses; 新 AI 产品想被采用，可能得先接进主流 harness
sections.body:
I receive around 3-5 requests to test a new AI product daily. Almost all of them require creating a new account and logging into a separate website or app.

Meanwhile, I basically only use ChatGPT, Grok, etc to do everything on my computer and browser.

These harnesses already have all my context and I don't want to start over from scratch with a new website or tool that only understands a small slice of my data. 

So with a few exceptions, the new products that I'm mostly likely to adopt need to work in today's top AI harnesses.

I realize only a small segment of users behave this way but I bet this segment will expand drastically soon.

我每天大概会收到 3 到 5 个测试新 AI 产品的请求。几乎每一个都要我新建账号，再登录一个单独的网站或 app。

但与此同时，我基本上只用 **ChatGPT**、**Grok** 之类的东西来处理我电脑和浏览器上的所有事。

这些 harness 已经有我全部的上下文了，我不想为了一个只懂我少量数据的新网站或工具，再从零开始。

所以除少数例外，我最可能采用的新产品，得能在当下这些主流 AI harness 里工作。

我知道现在这么用的人还只是小部分，但我赌这个群体很快会明显变大。

sections.headline: Enterprise AI leaders are told to stay model-agnostic; 企业 AI 负责人被建议把栈做成模型无关
sections.body:
If you lead AI for an enterprise, the highest leverage thing you can do is to make your AI stack model agnostic. 

There are two things I would invest in.

1/ Today: build an eval suite that fully captures your use cases and business outcomes. Most companies I’ve seen do not do a good job of this.

2/ Within the next year: build the capability to post-train open models. The talent gap here is even more acute, so start planning today.

This gives you the flexibility to switch models, customize them, compare them on your own workloads, and optimize for the best combination of quality, cost and latency.

own the evals, own the models.

如果你在企业里负责 AI，杠杆最高的一件事，就是把你的 AI 技术栈做成模型无关。

有两件事我会投。

1/ 现在就做：搭一套真正覆盖你业务场景和结果指标的 eval suite。就我看到的，大多数公司这块做得都不够。

2/ 未来一年内：建立对开源模型做后训练的能力。这方面的人才缺口更大，所以今天就该开始准备。

这样你就能灵活切模型、做定制、拿自家负载比较，还能把质量、成本和延迟一起优化。

把 evals 握在自己手里，把模型能力也握在自己手里。

sections.headline: An internal **WebGPU** tool becomes an agent-native devtool; 内部 **WebGPU** 技术被做成面向 agent 的开发工具
**Software** and **agents** are framed as a joint expansion story; **软件** 和 **agents** 被说成是一条一起长大的曲线
sections.body:
This week’s tech earnings calls were a critical reminder of how valuable the relationship is between software and AI.

Software provides the guardrails for how data is managed, how business logic in workflows are maintained, how you manage and govern access to information, how you protect data, and more. You want these systems to work the same way every time, without fail. 

Agents, on the other hand, work inside these systems and with this data to execute on tasks just like people would have. But at a scale far greater than people ever did, which is especially why the deterministic controls matter more than ever.  

And in fact many of the best ways to deploy agents will be directly within the software systems themselves, like from Salesforce, Box, Harvey, ServiceNow, and so on. These platforms can optimize agents for their workflows and domains, with evals and context that are unique to their vertical, as well as connect to other 
 agents headlessly. 

The net result is both software and AI adoption go up, hand in hand. Software and Agents are going to work together, and ultimately grow the size of the IT TAM dramatically as a result over time.

这周科技公司财报电话会再次提醒人一件事：软件和 AI 之间的关系，非常值钱。

**软件** 提供的是护栏，决定数据怎么管、工作流里的业务逻辑怎么维持、信息访问怎么治理、数据怎么保护，等等。这些系统必须每次都按同样的方式稳定运行。

另一边，**agents** 则是在这些系统里、拿着这些数据去执行任务，就像人一样，只是规模远超以往。也正因为规模上来了，确定性的控制反而更重要。

而且很多最好的 agent 落地方式，本来就会直接长在软件系统内部，比如 **Salesforce**、**Box**、**Harvey**、**ServiceNow** 这些平台。它们可以围绕自己的工作流和垂直场景去优化 agent，也能用本行业特有的 evals 和上下文，还能无头连接别的 agents。

最后的结果会是：软件和 AI 的采用一起往上走。**Software** 和 **Agents** 会一起工作，也会把整个 IT TAM 越做越大。

sections.headline: Signal’s disappearing messages meet screenshot reality; **Signal** 阅后即焚，还是挡不住截图现实
sections.body:
The funniest thing about Silicon Valley group chats is that

a) everyone uses Signal with disappearing messages on 

but 

b) everyone also screenshots and sends these messages around in (sometimes) non-ephemeral channels

Like, what are we doing here friends? 😂

硅谷群聊最好笑的一点是：

a）大家都用开着阅后即焚的 **Signal**

但是

b）大家又会把这些消息截图，转发到别的频道里（有时还不是阅后即焚）

朋友们，我们这到底是在干嘛？ 😂

sections.headline: **Claude** opens a discounted science team plan for 10,000 researchers; **Claude** 面向 1 万名科研人员推出折扣团队计划
sections.body:
Starting today, 10,000 scientists across every field, from math to chemistry to physics and more, can get Claude through our new Claude Team plan for scientists. Standard seats are free, and premium seats with 5x usage limits are $15 per month, an 80% discount, for one year.

Claude is becoming increasingly capable of scientific work, with recent progress on problems from advanced physics calculations to protein design. Alongside that progress, we've been investing in the research community: Claude Science launched in June, and our AI for Science program funds high-impact projects with free credits. Today's expansion builds on both.

Principal investigators (or equivalent) at academic and nonprofit research institutions can sign up, then add the researchers in their group. Over the coming months, we plan to extend the program well beyond the initial 10,000 seats.

Learn more: https://t.co/RTG1JxWi4Q

从今天开始，数学、化学、物理等各个领域的 10,000 名科学家，都可以通过我们新的面向科研人员的 **Claude Team** 计划使用 **Claude**。标准席位免费，高级席位每月 15 美元，使用额度是 5 倍，首年打 8 折。

**Claude** 在科学工作上的能力还在持续变强，最近已经能处理从高级物理计算到蛋白质设计这类问题。与此同时，我们也一直在投研究社区：**Claude Science** 在 6 月上线，**AI for Science** 项目则用免费额度资助高影响力项目。今天这次扩展，正是接着这两条线往下走。

高校和非营利研究机构的 PI（或同等角色）现在可以报名，再把自己组里的研究人员加进来。接下来几个月，我们计划把这个项目远远扩到最初的 10,000 个席位之外。

了解更多： https://t.co/RTG1JxWi4Q
